Understanding Secure English Language Tests

We already know that Secure English Language Tests are standardised English proficiency tests that assess an applicant’s ability to use English in real-world scenarios. These tests are designed to assess a person’s speaking, reading, writing, and listening English language skills.

Recognised SELT Providers

A lot of providers conduct SELT tests in the UK and outside. Here are the most common ones:

  • IELTS, or the International English Language Testing System, is offered in 140 countries and accepted by over 10,000 organisations.
  • TOEFL iBT, or the Test of English as a Foreign Language, is offered in over 165 countries and accepted by over 9,000 organisations.
  • PTE Academic or the Pearson Test of English Academic is offered in over 50 countries and accepted by over 7,000 organisations.

SELT Tests and Proficiency Levels    

  • Commonly accepted SELT tests: There are many language proficiency SELT tests, but the commonly accepted ones include IELTS, TOEFL iBT, and PTE Academic. These tests are accepted by more than 10,000 organisations in the world, including the UK Home Office, the US Department of State, and the Canadian government.

SELT Providers And Test Formats

There are many SELT assessment providers, but three of them are the most popular and are taken by applicants worldwide. They are:

  • IELTS
  • TOEFL iBT
  • PTE Academic

All these providers have their own assessment criteria and scoring systems. As an applicant, you can take any of these tests to determine your English language proficiency.

Test Formats and Components

All the SELT assessments are designed to assess your English language proficiency in four key areas. They are:

  • Speaking: The speaking test is conducted by a one-on-one interview with a trained examiner. The examiner will ask various questions about yourself, your work, your interests, and a variety of topics. You will also be given a task like describing a picture.
  • Listening: This test is conducted through a series of recordings. You will be asked to listen to the recordings and answer questions from those recordings on a variety of topics, such as conversations, news reports, and lectures.
  • Reading: The reading test will have a series of texts you have to read out. You will be given several texts and answer questions from them. The texts might be in the form of articles, letters, or anything else.
  • Writing: The writing test consists of several assessments, such as writing an essay, a letter, or any other formal or informal writing.

Test Duration and Scheduling Options

The duration of your SELT assessment varies based on which test you are choosing. Different providers have different durations of their tests. For example, the IELTS UKVI test takes about 2 hours and 45 minutes to complete.

Each of these providers offers multiple test schedules throughout the year. You can book a schedule with your chosen provider over the phone or by email. 

Test Fees and Payment Methods

The test fees also depend on which provider you choose and the test level. For example, secure English language tests for UKVI IELTS cost GBP 181.25. You can pay the provider using credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal.

Preparing For A SELT

Here’s how you can take an all-out preparation for an SELT assessment:

  • Familiarising yourself with the test format: This is the first preparation you need to take for a SELT assessment. Different SELT assessment has different formats. Knowing the test format includes knowing the question patterns, test durations, and how to answer the questions.
  • Understanding the assessment criteria: You must know the assessment criteria of SELT tests. This way, you can determine which provider you will select to take the final test. You will find this information on the test provider’s website.
  • Practising test components: This is the most crucial part of your test preparation. You need to practice four key components of the assessment: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Practising them several times will give you the confidence to demonstrate these skills in the examination hall. Several resources are available to practice these modules.
  • Utilising study materials and resources: You will find many study materials and resources to prepare well for the assessment. Some of these materials are available online on websites and apps.
  • Mock tests and simulations: Another good way to prepare yourself better for the assessment is by taking mock tests and simulations. They will help you practice the modules under timed conditions.

Booking And Taking A SELT

Secure English Language test SELT is a standardised test with a specific format. Taking an SELT assessment includes several stages. Let’s discuss the process of booking and taking an SELT test. 

  • Registering for the test: The first step of taking an SELT is to register for the test. First, you must choose a provider and register with them on an available date. Online registration is available, or you can do that by phone call as well. 
  • Selecting a suitable test location: You do not want to go far away from your home to take the test. That's why you should choose a test centre that is located in a suitable location for you. Make sure to select from approved secure English language test centres.
  • Booking the test date and time: After selecting a suitable test centre, you can book your SELT test date and time. Typically, you will have multiple dates and times to choose from.
  • Test day instructions and requirements: On your test day, you must bring your identification and documentation with you. Make sure to follow the test centre's instructions.
  • Identification and documentation: The SELT test requires two types of identification. One is a photo ID, such as your passport. The other one can be your birth certificate or your student ID.
  • Test centre facilities and support: You can expect several facilities from the test centre, such as a quiet room, a fast internet connection, a proper climate system, proper lighting, etc.

Receiving And Reporting Test Results

Test Results Timeline

The results of the SELT test are usually available within 13 days of the test. However, the timeline can vary based on the test provider and your centre. To learn more about results and other information, contact your test provider.

Understanding SELT Score Reports

SELT score reports are given as a detailed breakdown of your performance on each test module. It also includes your overall SELT score. By looking at the score, you can understand your strengths and weaknesses in English proficiency.

Validity of SELT Results

SELT assessment has a specific validity, which is 2 years. It means your SELT score will be valid for up to 2 years from taking the assessment. After that, you will have to retake the test to demonstrate your proficiency.

Reporting Test Results to Relevant Authorities

Retaking A SELT

If you are dissatisfied with your score or more than two years have passed since your assessment, you can retake the SELT test.

  • Reasons for retaking a SELT: There are several reasons you can retake a SELT. If you did not pass the test, you want to improve your score, and your score validity is over.
  • Waiting periods between test attempts: it depends on the test provider. Some providers allow retaking as soon as the result is out. Others require you to wait for some time.
  • Test registration and booking process for retakes: the process is exactly similar to that of first-timers. You will have to create an account, take a test date, and pay the re-take fee.
